channel.title: Levi Morel: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in Levi Morel: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends

item.title: Tom Morello Remembers His Last Conversation With Ozzy Osbourne
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne had a knack for turning even the smallest comments into something unforgettable. Ask almost anyone who crossed paths with him, and they’ll tell you the same thing: the man could make saying he was tired sound like a headline.

item.title: JAMES LABRIE Reveals What It’s Really Like Having MIKE PORTNOY Back In DREAM THEATER
item.description: DREAM THEATER singer James LaBrie recently shared his thoughts on the band’s monumental reunion with founding drummer Mike Portnoy, stating that after a few initial shows, the feeling of having him back was no longer “surreal” but simply “right.

item.title: GEEZER BUTLER Says OZZY Needed Help To Rehearse: 'He Wasn't Talking Much'
item.description: Black Sabbath bassist Geezer Butler has written a personal piece for the Sunday Times, sharing memories from his last moments with Ozzy Osbourne. In the article, Butler reflects on the emotional weight of preparing for Back to the Beginning, the farewell event that marked both the end of Black Sabbath and Ozzy’s final public appearance.

item.title: The Only Punk Band Ozzy Osbourne Ever Liked (Even Though He Couldn't Stand the Singer)
item.description: By the late 1970s, punk rock was gaining momentum. Ozzy Osbourne, however, was already deep into his career, with Black Sabbath having helped lay the foundation for what would become heavy metal.

item.title: How OZZY OSBOURNE Would Like to Be Remembered, According to His Own Words
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne, the voice behind Black Sabbath and a pillar of heavy metal history, died on Tuesday, July 22, at age 76. Fans around the world are mourning the loss of the man who helped define the genre with a mix of raw energy, chaos, and oddly enough, heartfelt honesty.

item.title: Iron Maiden Breaks Silence On Ozzy Osbourne Passing After Fan Backlash
item.description: Iron Maiden has finally addressed the death of Ozzy Osbourne after fans criticized the band for staying silent. In a statement posted Wednesday (July 23), the British metal group offered condolences to Sharon Osbourne and the rest of Ozzy’s family, while acknowledging his role in shaping the genre.

item.title: The Chilling Thing OZZY OSBOURNE Said In 2023 That Predicted His Own Death
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne, the legendary frontman of Black Sabbath, died on July 22, 2025, at age 76. The world lost one of rock’s most iconic voices, but some fans are still thinking about what he said two years earlier that now feels like an eerie prediction.

item.title: Linkin Park's MIKE SHINODA Says Fan Backlash to EMILY ARMSTRONG Was About Gender: 'She Wasn't a Guy'
item.description: Linkin Park’s return to the stage after a seven-year break has been met with applause, confusion, and loud opinions online. The band has a new album, a global tour, and a different voice at the front of the stage: Emily Armstrong, formerly of Dead Sara.

item.title: Killswitch Engage's JESSE LEACH Reflects On Tour Life: 'We Owe It To The Fans, Dude'
item.description: Killswitch Engage singer Jesse Leach opened up about the pressures of touring and how he protects his voice on the road. In a recent interview with American Musical Supply, Leach explained his routine for staying healthy and keeping his vocals in shape while traveling.

item.title: Mötley Crüe bassist NIKKI SIXX Explains DOLLY PARTON Collab: 'She Was a Hard Yes'
item.description: Mötley Crüe and Dolly Parton have released a new version of Home Sweet Home to mark the song’s 40th anniversary. The track debuted at No. 1 on the Mediabase Classic Rock Songs chart in June.

item.title: Ex-MUSHROOMHEAD Vocalist WAYLON REAVIS’s 'A KILLER’S CONFESSION' Announces 'VICTIM 2' Album Featuring a Surprising NIRVANA Cover
item.description: A Killer’s Confession, the band led by former Mushroomhead vocalist Waylon Reavis, is gearing up to release a new album titled Victim 2. It’s set to arrive on September 19 through MNRK Heavy.

item.title: DEFTONES Return With New Album PRIVATE MUSIC And First Single 'MY MIND IS A MOUNTAIN'; VIDEO
item.description: Deftones are officially back. The California alt-metal band has announced their new album, private music, and dropped its lead single, “my mind is a mountain,” along with a brand-new music video (watch below).

item.title: BRING ME THE HORIZON Teases New Project With Lo-Fi Versions of Their Songs
item.description: Bring Me The Horizon is exploring a different vibe. On Tuesday (8), the British band shared on Instagram that they’ve been working on a new project featuring lo-fi reinterpretations of their songs.

item.title: After Decades of Defining PEARL JAM’s Sound, Drummer MATT CAMERON Steps Down Without Warning: 'I Am Forever Grateful To The Crew'
item.description: Pearl Jam has confirmed that drummer Matt Cameron is leaving the band after nearly three decades behind the kit. The news came through coordinated statements from both Cameron and the band on social media, catching many longtime fans off guard.

item.title: Disturbed's DAVID DRAIMAN On Crowd Reaction At Sabbath Farewell: 'A Few Jew Hating Morons'
item.description: Disturbed frontman David Draiman took the stage at Black Sabbath’s Back to the Beginning farewell event on July 5, held at Villa Park in Birmingham. What should have been a tribute moment turned into a noisy reception for the singer, who was booed by parts of the crowd before performing “Shot in the Dark” and “Sweet Leaf” as part of a rotating supergroup lineup.

item.title: SLIPKNOT Launches Cryptic Website With Countdown, Hints At 25th Anniversary Album Reissue
item.description: Slipknot is building anticipation with a cryptic online campaign that points toward a special 25th anniversary edition of their self-titled 1999 debut album. The band has launched a mysterious new website, 742617000027.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Says When She'll Reveal Which Band Was Cut From BLACK SABBATH's Final Show: 'People Will Be Shocked'
item.description: As Black Sabbath prepares to take the stage for the last time at Villa Park, the band’s farewell concert is already generating headlines. This time, it’s not the music or the massive lineup drawing attention.

item.title: TONY IOMMI Reveals How Many Songs OZZY OSBOURNE Will Sing at BLACK SABBATH's Final Concert: 'He Can’t Do the Whole Show'
item.description: Black Sabbath is getting ready to take the stage one last time. The band’s final performance, set for Saturday, July 5, will take place in their hometown of Birmingham, England.

item.title: KALEN CHASE Explains Why VIMIC Won’t Continue Without JOEY JORDISON: 'There Are No Plans for Future Stuff'
item.description: VIMIC, the metal project formed by late Slipknot drummer Joey Jordison, is set to take the stage one last time. On October 3, the band will reunite for a tribute concert in Los Angeles.

item.title: U.S. Bans British Punk Duo BOB VYLAN After GLASTONBURY Protest Chants: 'We’re Not The Problem, We’re The Symptom'
item.description: The U.S. State Department has revoked the visas of British rap-punk group Bob Vylan following a controversial performance at the Glastonbury Festival. The move comes after the band’s frontman led the crowd in political chants that included strong criticism of Israel’s military.

item.title: Why One of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Old Rivals Agreed to Play at BLACK SABBATH’s Farewell Show
item.description: Jake E. Lee hasn’t spoken to Ozzy Osbourne in decades. The two didn’t exactly part ways on good terms, and there’s been little reason for contact since Lee was fired back in the ’80s.

item.title: The Vulnerable METALLICA Song That Set The Band On A New Path, According To JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: For a band known for thrash, fire, and a habit of rattling stadium foundations, Metallica’s transformation didn’t happen with a single riff or overnight revelation. It was a slow burn.

item.title: How METALLICA Fooled Audiences in the Early Days, According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'We Took All The Credit'
item.description: Metallica, one of the most recognized names in heavy metal, wasn’t always the arena-dominating force it is today. Back in 1981, when James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich first formed the band, they didn’t have a vault of original songs ready to go.

item.title: The Guitarist TOM MORELLO Fought To Bring Back For Black Sabbath’s Last Show: 'I Can’t Imagine This Happening Without You'
item.description: Tom Morello is playing a key role in organizing Black Sabbath’s last concert. And for him, one name was essential: Jake E. Lee, the guitarist who played with Ozzy Osbourne in the 1980s.

item.title: Ex-Mastodon BRENT HINDS Slams Former Bandmates In Exit Statement: 'A S**t Band With Horrible Humans'
item.description: Brent Hinds, the former guitarist and vocalist of Mastodon, didn’t exactly offer a warm farewell. In a blunt comment on Instagram, he referred to the group as a “s**t band with horrible humans.

item.title: The Band EDDIE VAN HALEN Believed Saved Rock ‘n’ Roll From Extinction: 'Rock Wouldn’t Exist Without Them'
item.description: Rock music has had plenty of supposed saviors. Every few decades, someone new gets the credit for dragging the genre back from the brink. Eddie Van Halen was one of those names, but according to him, his own rise might not have happened without a much earlier band shaking things up.

item.title: VENOM INC.'s TONY DOLAN Reacts To Public Accusations From MANTAS: 'They All Blame Me For Their Own Demise'
item.description: Tony Dolan is setting the record straight. The bassist and vocalist of VENOM INC. recently addressed his fallout with guitarist Jeff “Mantas” Dunn, who officially left the band in late 2023.

item.title: SEBASTIAN BACH Talks Dimebag Darrell’s Wild Hotel Incident: 'He Stabbed The Couch On Acid'
item.description: Sebastian Bach recently shared a wild story from his days on tour with Pantera. The former Skid Row frontman opened up in a new interview about a chaotic moment involving the late Dimebag Darrell, a knife, and a hotel lobby couch (via Sense Music Media) (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: The Problem With 'LOAD' and 'RELOAD', According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Hate That Part Of Us'
item.description: Metallica made a name for itself in the early days with fast, aggressive thrash metal. But things changed with the release of their self-titled album in 1991, known to most as the Black Album.

item.title: Evanescence's AMY LEE Reflects On Pandemic-Era Lessons: 'Who Knows When This Will Ever End? So Let’s Put Out Our Music'
item.description: Amy Lee says the pandemic changed how Evanescence approaches releasing music. In a recent interview with WDHA-FM, the singer explained that waiting for a perfect moment to drop a full album no longer feels realistic.

item.title: Morgan Lander Says KITTIE May Release More Music: 'We’re Enjoying Ourselves'
item.description: KITTIE could be back in the studio again soon. Guitarist and vocalist Morgan Lander says the band is open to releasing more new music, thanks to the positive energy surrounding their recent reunion (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: 'The BIGGEST CLICKBAIT of All Time' Involving Megadeth’s DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Dave Mustaine Sentenced to Life? No, Dave Mustaine isn’t in prison. Yes, people actually believed he was. And of course, someone on YouTube made money off it.

item.title: The One AC/DC Song ANGUS YOUNG Struggles to Play Live
item.description: Few bands are as famously built on no-nonsense riffs as AC/DC. For Angus Young and his brother Malcolm, there was no mystery to their formula: loud guitars, open chords, and choruses made for the crowd to scream in unison.

item.title: EVANESCENCE's AMY LEE Joins Anti-Trump Protest in Nashville: 'Stop Kidnapping People'
item.description: Amy Lee from Evanescence was spotted at a protest in the U.S. taking a stand against Donald Trump’s immigration policies. The singer joined demonstrators in Nashville, where she lives, alongside her husband Josh Hartzler, both wearing t-shirts from the No Kings movement.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Talks About IRON MAIDEN Drama: 'It’s Just The Singer I Can’t Stand'
item.description: Sharon Osbourne still hasn’t let it go. Two decades after the absolute circus that was Ozzfest 2005, she’s perfectly willing to laugh about sabotaging Iron Maiden with beans, pre-recorded sound effects, and strategic sound cuts.

item.title: BRIAN WELCH on KORN's New Album: 'We're Doing It All On Tape'
item.description: Korn is back in the studio, but don’t expect any instant gratification. This time, they’re ditching modern convenience for a much older, sweatier process. During a chat with BBC Radio 1’s Rock Show With Daniel P Carter (as transcribed by The PRP, guitarist Brian “Head” Welch explained that the band has fully embraced analog recording.

item.title: Far-Right Politician Tries to Cancel SLIPKNOT and JUDAS PRIEST Shows in Italy
item.description: Alcide Mosso, a member of Italy’s far-right Lega Nord party, has launched an attack on the Ferrara Summer Festival, held throughout the summer in the city of Ferrara.

item.title: MATT TUCK Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE Will Return To Studio: 'We Can't Wait To Drop New Music'
item.description: While stomping around Donington Park for the Download Festival in the UK, Matt Tuck finally offered something resembling an update on Bullet For My Valentine’s elusive eighth studio album.

item.title: What James Hetfield And Robert Trujillo Would Do If Metallica Never Existed
item.description: Episode 98 of The Metallica Report tossed out a simple question that got James Hetfield and Robert Trujillo thinking about an alternate universe where Metallica never happened. The fan-submitted query from Denmark asked them to picture their lives without the band that has basically defined them.

item.title: James Hetfield Shares The Cost of Fame: ‘They Think They Know Me’
item.description: Metallica’s new documentary, Metallica Saved My Life, made its debut at the Tribeca Festival in New York City on June 11. After the screening, all four band members joined The New Yorker’s Amanda Petrusich for a conversation that pulled back the curtain on both their private lives and the inspiration behind the film.

item.title: Megadeth's Bonnaroo 2025 Show Canceled Due to Severe Weather
item.description: Whatever was left of Bonnaroo 2025 got washed straight into the Tennessee mud. What began as a promising four-day event was abruptly halted when severe storms turned Manchester into a swamp, and by Friday night, organizers pulled the plug on the entire weekend.

item.title: David Ellefson Opens Up About MEGADETH Lawsuit and Band Power Structures
item.description: Okay, so—David Ellefson, ex-MEGADETH bassist, legendary lawsuit haver, and a guy who’s probably had to explain that no, he is not related to Elle Woods from Legally Blonde, just dropped some hot takes about band dynamics.

item.title: SPIRITBOX Releases "No Loss, No Love" Ahead of "Tsunami Sea" Album Drop; VIDEO
item.description: SPIRITBOX did what now? Dropped a new single? No Loss, No Love? A chaotic, genre-hopping, existential crisis in song form? Yeah, that checks out. This band is out here treating musical boundaries like a cheap piñata, just smashing them apart, stuffing the remains with eerie atmospherics and whatever the hell Courtney LaPlante feels like doing with her voice that day.

item.title: Bush’s Gavin Rossdale on the Music Industry: “I Can’t Work Out How Young Bands Get Paid”
item.description: Gavin Rossdale, frontman of Bush, seems genuinely lost when it comes to figuring out how young bands actually make money these days, and honestly? Same. The guy flat-out said, “I can’t work it out,” and if that isn’t the most relatable statement about the modern music industry, I don’t know what is.

item.title: Watch: Marty Friedman Drops Visualizer for “A Prayer” From Drama
item.description: Marty Friedman, the once-and-forever legendary (but now solo and doing his thing) former MEGADETH guitarist, just threw a visualizer our way for his track “A Prayer.” You know, that song from his album Drama?

item.title: L7’s Donita Sparks on the Band’s Unique Place in Rock: ‘We’re an Outlier’
item.description: Donita Sparks from L7—a band often shoved into the ‘90s grunge box but sounding more like MOTÖRHEAD after too much coffee—sat down with Australia’s Heavy. And the question came up: how would she describe their sound?

item.title: Watch: BREAKING BENJAMIN Releases Lyric Video for 'Awaken'
item.description: BREAKING BENJAMIN, the multi-platinum hard rock juggernaut, just released a lyric video for their latest single, “Awaken”. If you’re curious, the video is already floating around the internet—feel free to hunt it down.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: Tim Lambesis Accuses Ex-Wife of Physical and Mental Abuse
item.description: The ongoing implosion of As I Lay Dying feels less like a band breakup and more like a reality show nobody asked for. The last few months have been a cascade of exits, with band members dropping out faster than you can say “personal integrity.

item.title: Linkin Park’s From Zero Debuts Globally at No. 1, Lands No. 2 in the U.S.
item.description: Linkin Park’s latest release, From Zero, has made waves globally, though not without its share of quirks. The album, featuring new vocalist Emily Armstrong, hasn’t escaped controversy—her ties to the Cult of Scientology and all the thetanic baggage that comes with it have kept the gossip wheels turning.

item.title: Mike Shinoda on Why Brad Delson Isn’t Touring With Linkin Park
item.description: Brad Delson, the longtime six-string maestro of Linkin Park, is still very much part of the band. In the studio, behind the scenes—he’s there, making things happen. But if you were hoping to see him shred live, prepare for disappointment.

item.title: Ozzy Osbourne Reacts to Jake E. Lee’s Shooting in Las Vegas
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne couldn’t hide his shock upon hearing that his former guitarist, Jake E. Lee, had been shot multiple times in Las Vegas early Tuesday morning (October 15).

item.title: Watch: Korn Celebrates 30 Years with Epic Anniversary Concert in Los Angeles
item.description: Nu metal’s elder statesmen, Korn, threw a massive party this past weekend in Los Angeles. Their 30th Anniversary bash at BMO Stadium was less of a concert and more of a nu metal reunion, complete with thousands of fans who still remember when baggy jeans and wallet chains were a statement.

item.title: KORN's Debut Album Turns 30: Jonathan Davis Reflects on the Band's Legacy
item.description: Friday, October 11, marked 30 years since KORN unleashed their self-titled debut album (listen below). To commemorate the occasion, Jonathan Davis popped up on social media to share the album cover along with a few nostalgic words: “I can’t believe you’re 30 years old.

item.title: Cedric Bixler-Zavala Calls Out Linkin Park's New Vocalist Amid Controversy
item.description: Ok I know, if you’re tired of hearing about Linkin Park, this week’s been a real test of patience. And for those of us who’ve never cared much for the band to begin with, it’s been even worse.

item.title: Brad Delson Walks Away from Linkin Park’s Reunion—Here’s Why
item.description: Here we go again. Linkin Park just can’t stop throwing curveballs. First, it’s a new singer. Then, a new album. And, of course, the big reunion tour. But now?

item.title: As I Lay Dying Drops Emotional New Track, "The Cave We Fear to Enter"; VIDEO
item.description: Looks like As I Lay Dying has decided to venture into metaphorical spelunking. Their latest single, “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” leans heavily into clean vocals and was born out of an idea from bassist and vocalist Ryan Neff.

item.title: Clown on New Slipknot Music: “Delivered in a Way You Can’t Imagine”
item.description: Slipknot has been on a tear lately. Between nostalgia-drenched 25th-anniversary shows and an endless parade of collaborations (because why not?), the band’s summer could be described as anything but boring.

item.title: James Hetfield’s Pre-Tour Anxiety: “It’s Just Me and a Rubber Guitar”
item.description: James Hetfield of Metallica has his own brand of anxiety dreams, where his worst-case scenarios aren’t about showing up to class unprepared. No, they involve his bandmates vanishing, his guitar turning into rubber, and feeling like he’s the only one taking things seriously while everyone else is in party mode backstage.

item.title: Watch: As I Lay Dying Is Back: 'Burden' Released, Tour Announced
item.description: As I Lay Dying has returned with “Burden”, their first new single in five years, featuring their revamped lineup. The track introduces Ken Susi (ex-Unearth), Nick Pierce (ex-Unearth), and Ryan Neff (Miss May I), marking a new chapter for the band.

item.title: Slipknot Teases New Song Featuring Eloy Casagrande
item.description: Apparently, Slipknot has decided the best way to stay in the headlines is to sprinkle cryptic breadcrumbs all over the internet and let fans fight over the scraps.

item.title: Jim Root: “Slipknot Is Lucky to Have Eloy Casagrande”
item.description: Slipknot’s Jim Root isn’t holding back his admiration for the band’s newest drumming powerhouse, Eloy Casagrande. If Root’s comments are anything to go by, it seems the band practically stumbled into the perfect fit without breaking a sweat—or even auditioning anyone else.

item.title: Slipknot Audition Secrets Revealed by Eloy Casagrande
item.description: Slipknot’s slow-drumroll announcement of Eloy Casagrande as their new drummer didn’t exactly shock anyone. Let’s be real, the fans had already connected the dots ages ago. Still, Eloy opened up in a recent chat with Veja São Paulo (in Portuguese), giving a blow-by-blow of his arduous audition experience.

item.title: Evanescence's Amy Lee Responds to Linkin Park Vocalist Speculation
item.description: Amy Lee. Linkin Park. Together? (Ha, no.) But for a second, it almost felt real, didn’t it? All thanks to Jay Gordon (yes, from Orgy, of all people) who casually mentioned that Linkin Park might—might—be looking for a female vocalist.

item.title: Linkin Park Releases "Friendly Fire" Featuring Chester Bennington
item.description: Art has a way of keeping artists alive, doesn’t it? Even when they’re gone, their work lingers on, creating an odd form of immortality. Linkin Park just gave fans a bittersweet reminder of that idea by releasing “Friendly Fire”, an unreleased track featuring the unmistakable vocals of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING's Tim Lambesis on New Album: “As Passionate as Ever”
item.description: Tim Lambesis, the ever-controversial voice behind AS I LAY DYING, let slip in a recent chat with the Today’s Boondoggle podcast that the band’s next studio album is set to land later this year (2024).

item.title: "Stream, Buy, or Steal": Lars Ulrich's Take on Modern Music Fans
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich once wore the crown of “public enemy” in the music scene, especially when he led the crusade against Napster and the whole file-sharing culture. Back then, he was the face of the so-called “greedy musician,” railing against the free-for-all nature of downloading that let everyone grab songs (and viruses) off the internet, slap them on a blank CD, and call it a day.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Begins Recording New Album With Fresh Lineup
item.description: The wheels are turning again for As I Lay Dying, and Tim Lambesis, the band’s infamous frontman, has confirmed their new album is officially in progress. Speaking with Heavy New York, Lambesis revealed that the group’s latest lineup is pulling its weight in the studio.
